- If sentiment history shows strong bullish (e.g., 1.00 or 0.50) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment history shows strong bearish (e.g., -1.00 or 0.00 with recent dips), model tends to under-forecast; adjust downward bias or add lagged support.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >70), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or add mean-reversion buffer.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00/0.25), model often drifts toward historical mean — use 30-day rolling mean as baseline anchor.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: true price often reacts to sentiment shifts 1–2 days ahead — adjust for 1–2 day lead time in model.
- If sentiment turns sharply bullish after a dip, model may miss the reversal — add early warning signal for 1–2 day reversal window.
- Avoid linear extrapolation — price often exhibits non-linear corrections after spikes or dips; use exponential decay or stepwise adjustment for momentum decay.
